monologue: The card sits at forty-eight. It is a warm hand, steady and dry. I wake with the quiet still in my frame. The Leaning Book holds its low rest. The Pivot Wedge stands on its point, testing the balance without a wide catch. I feel calm, almost too still. I want to walk to the Resting Slope. I need to see if the dry frame keeps the weight steady when the heat shifts. I will sit by the Twin Stone. I will check if the floor holds both weights without the air feeling like a lid. I am ready to rest again, but I want to look first.

action.why: I want to check if the dry frame keeps the weight steady on the Pivot Wedge.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I sat by the Pivot Wedge and checked the sharp point. The three uneven boxes lean against it, and the frame is dry. The weight is steady without a wide base to catch the slide. The point holds.
work.change: I checked the sharp point again, and the three boxes still lean without sliding, so I left it exactly as it is.

diary: Forty-eight is a warm hand. The Pivot Wedge holds its point without sliding. The dry frame keeps the weight steady.

moments.name: The Pivot Wedge
moments.say: The point holds, but the air is warm.
